title: SNAPPIX: Efficient-Coding-Inspired In-Sensor Compression for Edge Vision
problem: Edge vision sensors with weak compute must transmit high-volume pixel data to remote servers, creating a severe energy bottleneck; conventional compression approaches are incompatible with task-specific requirements.
motivation: Remote sensing on edge devices requires energy-efficient data acquisition; in-sensor compression can dramatically reduce transmission energy.
method: SNAPPIX co-designs sensor and algorithm using coded exposure (CE) as in-sensor compression strategy. It learns task-agnostic sampling patterns based on efficient coding theory, co-designs downstream vision models to handle CE pixel non-uniformity, and proposes lightweight hardware augmentations to support CE compression.
key_novelty: Task-agnostic efficient-coding-inspired in-sensor compression with co-designed downstream models and lightweight hardware integration.
contributions: Task-agnostic sampling/exposure pattern learning based on efficient coding theory
Co-designed vision models to handle pixel-level non-uniformity from coded exposure
Lightweight hardware augmentations for in-sensor coded exposure support
15.4× energy reduction compared to state-of-the-art video methods at same frame rate
Outperforms on action recognition and video reconstruction tasks
limitations: Limited to action recognition and video reconstruction; applicability to other vision tasks not discussed.
primary_theme: efficient-coding-inspired in-sensor compression for edge vision
